lines.text: Types of employment contracts.
A temporary contract [tijdelijk contract] is for a fixed period [bepaalde tijd], for example half a year; it contains an end date [einddatum].
A job is almost always temporary at first.
A permanent contract [vast contract] contains no end date.
After a maximum of three temporary contracts (or after three years), the next contract automatically becomes a permanent contract.
A contract through a temp agency is always temporary.
Working without paying tax is called working illegally [zwartwerken] ("black work"): that is forbidden [verboden], and then you have no insurance [verzekering] if something happens at work.
If you do pay tax, you have legal ("white") work.
What is in an employment contract?
Your rights [rechten] and duties [plichten] as an employee are in the contract.
Rights are the things the employer must do for you; duties are the things you must do.

Agreements about rights and duties are also called employment conditions [arbeidsvoorwaarden]: how many hours you work, when you start (and stop), your salary, whether you work independently or under supervision [begeleiding], agreements about working conditions [arbeidsomstandigheden] (safety, health, noise), how much holiday you get, and whether the employer pays your travel expenses [reiskosten].
The cao.
Cao means: collective labour agreement [collectieve arbeidsovereenkomst].
The cao contains agreements between all employers and employees of one sector (for example construction or hospitality).
Rights are, for example: the right to the minimum wage [minimumloon] (the lowest salary the employer must pay) and the right to salary when you are ill.
Duties are, for example: working the number of hours stated in your contract, and reporting when you are ill.
How does your employer evaluate you?
There is a registration [registratie] to see how much you work.
Sometimes you have a performance review [beoordelingsgesprek]: then your employer evaluates how you perform [functioneert].
You should prepare well for such a meeting; you can also raise topics yourself.
How can you have a say?
A works council [ondernemingsraad, OR] is a group of employees who may participate in decisions about the employer's plans.
In a company with more than fifty employees it is mandatory that employees participate in decision-making.
A participation council [medezeggenschapsraad, MR] is similar to an OR; at schools it also includes parents and teachers.
Employees can also become a member of the staff association [personeelsvereniging, PV]: it organises fun things, for example parties or excursions.
The trade union.
A trade union [vakbond] helps employees, for example in a conflict with an employer.
Trade unions also participate in decisions about the cao.
Examples are the FNV and the CNV.
As a member you pay money to the union every month.
Paying tax.
Your payslip [loonstrook, or salarisstrook] is a document showing your salary; you receive it every month or whenever something changes.
Once a year you receive an annual salary statement [jaaropgave] with your salary for that year.
It shows your gross salary [brutosalaris] and net salary [nettosalaris].
Example: you earn €2000 gross per month, you receive €1600 in the bank (net) and pay €400 in taxes and premiums.
You must keep your payslip for at least five years.
Paying premiums.
Premiums/contributions [premies] are what you pay for insurance.

From your salary you pay, for example: a premium for your pension [pensioen] (money for when you are too old to work; you only build up this work pension if you have worked — in addition, everyone living in the Netherlands receives AOW from the SVB from retirement age), a premium for if you become unemployed [werkloos], and a premium for if you become unfit for work [arbeidsongeschikt].
Your employer also pays premiums for you.
Starting your own business.
If you are an employee, you are in salaried employment [loondienst].
You can also become an independent entrepreneur [ondernemer], with your own staff [personeel], or a self-employed person without staff [zzp'er, zelfstandige zonder personeel].
You must then register with the Chamber of Commerce [Kamer van Koophandel, KvK].
The KvK helps businesses, provides information and courses and can help you with a business plan [ondernemersplan].
Independent entrepreneurs must arrange their own pension [pensioen] and take out disability insurance [arbeidsongeschiktheidsverzekering, AOV].
